atp-cycle.alt: A cycle with ATP at the top and ADP plus phosphate at the bottom. On the right, ATP hydrolysis releases energy that drives work: building molecules, pumping ions and moving muscle. On the left, energy from breaking down food molecules adds a phosphate back to ADP to make ATP. The same molecules are recycled over and over.

feedback-inhibition-pathway.alt: A pathway from molecule A to B to C to D, each step run by its own enzyme, numbered 1 to 3. A dashed line from the end product D loops back to enzyme 1, the first enzyme, and ends in a block symbol: D binds enzyme 1's allosteric site and slows step 1 when D builds up.
